purpose: Authoritative machine-checkable inventory of high-confidence production placeholders, status drift, and narrow approved exception classes for the runtime-placeholder eradication initiative. In phase 7 this file also serves as the concrete row inventory for the broader cutover scoreboard.

scoreboard_contract.scope: Concrete runtime placeholders, status drift, and operator-gap rows that must either be eliminated or explicitly quarantined before cutover closes.

approved_exception_classes.description: Placeholder, stub, and TODO markers may appear in non-shipping test or fuzz surfaces when the marker does not leak into runtime code paths.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: Runtime code, manifests, and operator paths must not depend on these markers or import their behavior as a live fallback.

approved_exception_classes.description: Shared mock infrastructure may use placeholder-like naming as test scaffolding only when it stays inside dedicated mock or fixture crates.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: Approved mock infrastructure must remain outside live runtime, catalog, and connector shipping paths.

approved_exception_classes.description: Benchmark fixture helpers may use stub naming only for synthetic offline microbench input construction, not for user-facing benchmark results.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: User-facing `fwc bench` commands must report real measurements; only internal offline fixture builders may retain stub terminology.

approved_exception_classes.description: Offline schema or template emitters may carry placeholder sentinel values when runtime install and update paths reject demo markers and generator regression tests keep emitted runtime code truthful.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: Any placeholder sentinel in an offline generator must stay off runtime execution paths and remain covered by generator regression tests.

approved_exception_classes.description: Documentation and evidence artifacts may quote placeholder strings as part of audits, transcripts, or remediation records.
approved_exception_classes.closure_rule: Quoted placeholder markers in docs or evidence must remain descriptive only and must not be presented as live runtime capability.

findings.title: Hugging Face manifest and runtime status disagree
findings.user_visible_impact: Operators and agents see contradictory manifest and runtime status for Hugging Face, so readiness and trust decisions are not mechanically reliable.
findings.replacement_path: Make the manifest, handshake, introspection, and catalog surfaces converge on the same live or explicitly quarantined status contract.
findings.deletion_gate: Close `flywheel_connectors-24llg.2.5` only after manifest, handshake, introspection, and catalog state agree on the same truthful status and the drift row is gone from the placeholder inventory.

unit: Manifest or catalog consistency checks proving the same status vocabulary is emitted everywhere.
integration: Connector or host integration coverage proving handshake and introspection stay aligned with manifest truth.
e2e: Operator-truth transcripts showing the connector no longer presents conflicting readiness or trust signals.

workflow_artifacts: Before: docs/testing/placeholder-scan.json row for huggingface-status-drift.
Before: transcript showing the old manifest/runtime disagreement.
After: refreshed transcript or replay bundle proving one truthful status contract across manifest and runtime surfaces.

findings.verification_expectation: Manifest or catalog consistency checks plus connector tests proving runtime and metadata status stay aligned.

findings.title: AWS connector still uses fake signing instead of SigV4
findings.user_visible_impact: AWS requests can look configured while still using fake header-based signing, so real service interaction is impossible or misleading.
findings.replacement_path: Adopt the shared SigV4 signer on the live request path and remove the fake `X-Aws-*` header fallback.
findings.deletion_gate: Close `flywheel_connectors-24llg.3.2` only after the fake `X-Aws-*` signing path is gone, the cross-cloud auth regression suite proves real SigV4 request signing, and the placeholder scan no longer reports this row.

unit: Canonical-request or signing tests proving real SigV4 material is produced for the live request path.
integration: AWS connector integration coverage proving real request signing on configured requests.
e2e: Cross-cloud auth regression artifacts proving the operator path no longer relies on fake headers.

workflow_artifacts: Before: placeholder-scan row and failing or placeholder auth transcript for AWS signing.
Before: current request trace showing fake `X-Aws-*` header fallback.
After: regression-script artifact bundle and connector transcript proving real SigV4 signing.
findings.rationale: Self-check and runtime messaging explicitly admit request signing is not implemented, and the client still sends raw `X-Aws-*` headers instead of canonical SigV4 signatures.
findings.exit_strategy: Adopt the shared SigV4 signer and replace the fake header path on real AWS requests.
findings.verification_expectation: Cross-cloud auth regression coverage plus connector verification proving real SigV4 request signing on the affected AWS surfaces.

findings.title: S3 presigned URLs still carry a placeholder signature
findings.user_visible_impact: Generated presigned S3 URLs remain unusable outside demo flows because the query signature is a literal placeholder.
findings.replacement_path: Replace placeholder presigning with real SigV4 query signing built on the shared canonical-request substrate.
findings.deletion_gate: Close `flywheel_connectors-24llg.3.3` only after presigned URLs carry real SigV4 query parameters, the placeholder signature literal is gone, and regression artifacts prove the generated URLs round-trip truthfully.

unit: Presign-path tests proving canonical query signing and expiry calculation are real rather than placeholder-backed.
integration: S3 connector integration coverage proving generated URLs are valid on the live code path.
e2e: Cross-cloud auth regression artifacts proving operator-facing presign output is no longer demo-only.

workflow_artifacts: Before: placeholder-scan row and transcript showing `PLACEHOLDER_SIGNATURE` in generated URLs.
Before: current presign trace or fixture demonstrating the placeholder branch.
After: regression-script artifact bundle and connector transcript proving real SigV4 query signing.
findings.rationale: The presign path still emits a literal `PLACEHOLDER_SIGNATURE` query component instead of a real SigV4 query signature.
findings.exit_strategy: Replace placeholder presigning with real SigV4 query signing backed by the shared canonical-request substrate.
findings.verification_expectation: Unit, integration, and connector-level verification that presigned URLs round-trip with real SigV4 query parameters.

unit: JWT bearer signing and token-exchange tests proving service-account mode is implemented rather than hard-refused.
integration: GCP connector integration coverage proving configured service-account flows succeed and fail truthfully.
e2e: Cross-cloud auth regression artifacts proving operator-visible service-account workflows are live and evidence-backed.

workflow_artifacts: Before: placeholder-scan row and transcript showing the hard refusal for service-account mode.
Before: current workflow trace demonstrating the unsupported path.
After: regression-script artifact bundle and connector transcript proving JWT bearer flow support.

findings.exit_strategy: Implement JWT bearer signing and token exchange for service-account mode instead of hard-refusing the path.

findings.title: Connector-state fork resolution still treats CRDT merge as a not-implemented placeholder
findings.user_visible_impact: Fork resolution can advertise CRDT merge as a strategy but still terminates at a not-implemented error, so recovery semantics remain incomplete.
findings.replacement_path: Implement real delta-level CRDT merge semantics for connector-state fork resolution instead of surfacing a placeholder strategy.
findings.deletion_gate: Close `flywheel_connectors-24llg.5.1` only after CRDT merge is a real recovery path, the not-implemented detector message is gone, and replayable fork-resolution artifacts prove the merged outcome is durable.

unit: CRDT merge tests proving delta-level merge semantics rather than placeholder failure.
integration: Fork-resolution scenarios proving recovery state is consistent across merge inputs and conflict shapes.
e2e: Replayable recovery artifacts proving operator-facing failover or recovery workflows no longer terminate at the placeholder path.

workflow_artifacts: Before: placeholder-scan row and transcript showing the CRDT merge placeholder failure.
Before: recovery scenario trace demonstrating the old detector message.
After: replay bundle or scenario transcript proving real merge-based recovery.
findings.rationale: Fork resolution records CRDT merge as a strategy but still fails with a not-implemented detector message rather than performing delta-level merge.
findings.exit_strategy: Implement real delta-level CRDT merge semantics for connector-state fork resolution.
findings.verification_expectation: Regression suites for fork resolution and CRDT merge semantics, including golden vectors or recovery scenarios.

findings.title: Mesh planner zone filtering is still a no-op placeholder
findings.user_visible_impact: Mesh placement can report zone filtering without actually narrowing candidate nodes, so scheduling and provenance claims are overstated.
findings.replacement_path: Plumb real node-zone data into placement filtering and reject the current no-op zoning path.
findings.deletion_gate: Close `flywheel_connectors-24llg.5.2` only after zone restrictions change candidate selection on the real planner path, the no-op placeholder is gone, and diagnostics prove why nodes were included or excluded.

unit: Planner tests proving node-zone information affects selection rather than acting as a no-op.
integration: Mesh integration coverage proving placement filtering changes candidate sets under zone policy.
e2e: No-mock or failover artifacts proving operator-visible placement claims match real zone-aware behavior.

workflow_artifacts: Before: placeholder-scan row and transcript showing zone filtering without candidate changes.
Before: placement trace demonstrating the current no-op zoning path.
After: integration transcript or replay bundle proving zone-aware placement and diagnostics.
findings.rationale: Placement planning still retains all candidates under zone restrictions because the planner lacks NodeInfo zone integration.
findings.exit_strategy: Plumb real node zone data into placement filtering and reject no-op zoning.
findings.verification_expectation: Zone-aware placement tests and diagnostics proving policy zone filters now change candidate selection truthfully.
